cards.claim: Bin Han spent a significant portion of his research career at the Instituto de Medicina Molecular (IMM).
cards.quote: Han's research career spans over two decades, with a significant portion of it spent at the Instituto de Medicina Molecular (IMM), a prestigious research institution affiliated with the University of Lisbon, in Lisbon, Portugal.

cards.claim: Bin Han was listed as a researcher at the School of Medicine, Sun Yat-sen University.
cards.quote: As we delve into the narrative of Bin Han's academic pursuits, a fascinating connection emerges – his affiliation with Sun Yat-sen University, a prestigious institution in Guangdong, China. The story begins with Bin Han's early research endeavors, which were marked by a series of publications and collaborations. A closer examination of his ORCID profile reveals a pattern of affiliations, with Sun Yat-sen University featuring prominently among them. This initial clue sets the stage for a deeper exploration of Bin Han's connection with the university. One of the earliest pieces of evidence dates back to 2015, when Bin Han co-authored a research paper titled "Investigating the Role of MicroRNAs in Cancer Development" (1). A scrutiny of the paper's author affiliations reveals that Bin Han was listed as a researcher at the School of Medicine, Sun Yat-sen University. This publication not only showcases Bin Han's expertise in the field of cancer research but also establishes a clear link between him and the university. Further investigation uncovers a series of research grants and projects that Bin Han was involved in, many of which were funded by Sun Yat-sen University.
